scope: CORRECTION: the landing field index is V-1, so the accepted body writes field 21 (an event codec), not field 22 - which explains why its ps is only 29 bits
the_key_correction: the landing index is `V - 1` (V is the target position and the landing is distance-1 from the previous position), so with V=22 the landing is index 21
index 21 in the 0xDA63E8 table is offset 268 / codec -94 (an EVENT codec), not offset 16 / codec 11
an empty event costs a single bit, which is exactly the 1 bit the body spends on its 'landing value'
whereas codec 11 (index 22) would cost a gate bit plus 11 value bits
so the accepted body does not touch origin[0] at all - it writes an event field, which is harmless by construction
why_this_matters: the long-standing assumption 'single22 writes field 22 = offset 16' was wrong by one index

every attempt to reach origin therefore aimed at V=23..23 with distance 23, which lands on index 22 only if the landing rule is distance-1 from position -1, i.e. distance 23 -> 22 - the two rules disagree and that ambiguity is what made the measurements incoherent
this round settles it in favour of V-1: the 29-bit fit only works for a single-bit landing value, i.e. an event codec
next: encode a body with V=23 and distance 23 so the landing is index 22 (codec 11, gate + 11 bits) and measure the ps length: the arithmetic now predicts 7 + 1 + 1 + 5 + 13 + 12 + 1 = 40 bits
if the measured length is 40, both the landing rule and the codec width are confirmed and origin[0] can actually be written
